__comment: Chain ingestion rules. A chain reacts to a committed write on trigger_table and projects it onto target_table through a mapper. | The production->inventory rule was removed with the demo tables it referenced (2026-08-01 fixture reset).

rules.__comment: dt_log -> dt_map: the DT map is DERIVED. dt_log is the record; the map is a projection of it, so nothing should ever write dt_map by hand -- a replay would then silently disagree with the hand-written rows. | SHIPS DISABLED and stays disabled this round by instruction. What was measured (2026-08-01): a chain CAN address a single map cell -- crud.apply_batch_updates composes the composite business key from the update payload itself (crud.py:1051-1059) when the caller omits business_key_val and supplies every composite_key_source column, and dt_map's composite key includes dt_x/dt_y, so one business key = one cell. What a chain CANNOT do is PURGE: replace_map lives on the batch (schemas.py:138) and chain_ingestion_worker.py:437-441 constructs the batch itself and never sets it, so a chain can only upsert cells and never delete stale ones. That is the open question, and it is why this stays off.
rules.name: dt_log_to_dt_map

rules.__comment: [NOT fixture data -- DO NOT DELETE AS DEAD] This table is not referenced by any fixture, so it looks unused. It is not. It exists because it is the only live exercise of the CHAIN path: test_api.py::test_chained_ingestion asserts on the outbox events the production_plan -> inventory_master chain produces, and removing these declarations silently removes that coverage. The dt_log_to_dt_map fixture chain cannot replace it -- that rule ships enabled:false on purpose (a chain can upsert map cells but cannot purge them), and turning an unsafe rule on to keep a test green is the same mistake as deleting the test. Its auto-update collector is disabled, so the table is declared but never grows. | The rule stays ENABLED so the test exercises the real worker path rather than a mock.
rules.name: production_to_inventory_reservation_batch
